claims.claim: PromptArena uses five main types of configuration files
Diagram node: arena.yaml is the Main Configuration (kind Arena)
Diagram node: PromptConfig is System Instructions
Diagram node: Scenario is Test Cases
Diagram node: Eval is Saved Conversation Evaluation
Diagram node: Provider is Model Config
Diagram node: Tool is Functions
Diagram node: Persona is Self-Play AI
Diagram edge: Arena references PromptConfig
Diagram edge: Arena references Scenario
Diagram edge: Arena references Eval
Diagram edge: Arena references Provider
Diagram edge: Arena references Tool
Diagram edge (dotted): Scenario references Persona
Example: the complete Arena structure block (every field and identifier used in lines 39-164) is valid
apiVersion is promptkit.altairalabs.ai/v1alpha1
kind is Arena
metadata.name is required
metadata.namespace is an optional field
metadata.labels is an optional key-value map
metadata.annotations is an optional non-identifying metadata map
spec.prompt_configs is a field
prompt_configs[].id is required (internal reference ID)
prompt_configs[].file is required (path to PromptConfig file)
prompt_configs[].vars is an optional field for template variable overrides
spec.providers is a field
providers[].group defaults to default
A provider with group judge is not used as the assistant
providers[].group is a field
spec.scenarios is a field
spec.evals is a field (saved conversation evaluation configs)
A judge inherits the model of the provider it maps to
spec.judges is a field
judges[].name is a field
judges[].provider is a field
spec.judge_defaults is a field
judge_defaults.prompt is a field
judge_defaults.prompt_registry is a field
spec.tools is an optional field
spec.mcp_servers is an optional list field
state_store is a top-level field, a sibling of defaults
state_store.type is a field
state_store.type enum values are memory, redis, file
state_store.type defaults to memory
state_store.redis is required when type is redis
state_store.redis.address is a field
state_store.file is required when type is file
state_store.file.root is a field
spec.defaults is a field (global defaults)
defaults.temperature is a field
defaults.temperature defaults to 0.7
defaults.max_tokens is a field
defaults.max_tokens default varies by provider
defaults.seed is an optional reproducibility seed
Omitting seed, or setting it to 0, sends no seed to the provider
defaults.concurrency is a field
defaults.concurrency defaults to 6; run -j overrides it
defaults.concurrency is the number of tests run in parallel
defaults.run_timeout is a field
defaults.run_timeout defaults to 5m
defaults.run_timeout applies per run
defaults.output is a field
defaults.output.dir is a field
defaults.output.dir defaults to out
defaults.output.formats is a field
defaults.output.formats defaults to [json]
defaults.output.formats enum values are json, markdown, junit
The json format has no configurable options and writes each result to <run-id>.json
defaults.output.markdown is a field
defaults.output.markdown.file is a field
defaults.output.markdown.file defaults to results.md
defaults.output.markdown.include_details is a field
defaults.output.markdown.include_details defaults to true
defaults.output.junit is a field
defaults.output.junit.file is a field
defaults.output.junit.file defaults to junit.xml, relative to output.dir
defaults.output.recording is a field
defaults.output.recording.enabled is a field
defaults.output.recording.enabled defaults to false
defaults.output.recording.dir is a field
defaults.output.recording.dir defaults to recordings
The recording dir is a subdirectory of output.dir
defaults.fail_on is a field
defaults.fail_on enum values are assertion_failure, provider_error, timeout, validation_error
prompt_configs[].id is a string and required; scenarios use it to reference the prompt
prompt_configs[].file is a required string; the path is relative to arena.yaml
prompt_configs[].vars is an optional object that overrides template variables declared with required: false
Variable precedence, highest to lowest: runtime variables, arena configuration (prompt_configs[].vars), prompt defaults
Runtime variables are passed at execution time via the SDK or CLI and take highest precedence
Arena configuration variables are defined in prompt_configs[].vars
Prompt defaults come from the PromptConfig variables array and apply to non-required variables
Example: arena.yaml prompt_configs entry (id support, file prompts/support.yaml, vars company_name, support_hours, support_email) is valid
Example: PromptConfig spec.variables block with name, type, required, default, description entries is valid
spec.variables is a field of PromptConfig
Each variables entry accepts name, type, required, default and description fields
spec.system_template is a field of PromptConfig
Placeholders such as {{company_name}} in system_template are substituted from the resolved variables
arena.yaml vars override prompt defaults, so the rendered template uses ACME Corp, 24/7 and help@acme.com
providers[].file is a required string field
Example: providers list with file entries is valid
scenarios[].file is a required string field
Example: scenarios list with file entries is valid
tools[].file is a required string field
Example: tools list with file entries is valid
Each mcp_servers entry has exactly one of command, url and source; a config with none or several fails to load
mcp_servers[].name is a required string used as the registry key
For stdio and url entries, name is the prefix of qualified tool names mcp__<name>__<tool>
mcp_servers[].timeout_ms is an optional integer per-request timeout in milliseconds
mcp_servers[].tool_filter is an optional object with allowlist and blocklist
The command transport spawns a local subprocess and speaks MCP over stdio
mcp_servers[].command is a required string (executable to run)
mcp_servers[].args is an optional string array
mcp_servers[].env is an optional string-to-string map whose ${VAR} references are replaced from the environment (empty when unset)
mcp_servers[].working_dir is an optional string
Example: stdio mcp_servers entry (npx, args, env NODE_ENV) is valid
A url server connects to an already-running server over one of two MCP HTTP transports, chosen with transport
mcp_servers[].url is a required string
What mcp_servers[].url points at depends on the transport
mcp_servers[].transport defaults to sse for a url server
mcp_servers[].transport enum values are sse and streamable_http
mcp_servers[].headers is an optional string map added to every request; ${VAR} references are replaced from the environment
With transport sse, url is the base URL
An sse server must serve GET /sse and POST /message?sessionId=...
The sse transport follows the MCP HTTP+SSE spec 2024-11-05
PromptArena appends /sse to the sse base URL itself
Pointing url at .../sse makes PromptArena request .../sse/sse
Example: url server with Authorization header is valid
With transport streamable_http, url is the full endpoint URL and is used as-is
The streamable_http transport follows the MCP Streamable HTTP spec 2025-03-26
Example: streamable_http url server is valid
A registered MCPSource opens its endpoint at a scope boundary and closes it when the boundary ends
Link: Provision an MCP Sandbox per Scenario guide at /arena/how-to/agents/provision-mcp-sandbox/
mcp_servers[].source is a required string naming a registered MCPSource
mcp_servers[].scope is required; enum values are run, scenario, session
mcp_servers[].source_args is an optional object of source-specific arguments
The built-in docker MCPSource is registered under the name docker
The docker source accepts the source_args key image
The docker source accepts the source_args key repo
The docker source accepts the source_args key branch
The docker source accepts the source_args key env
The docker source accepts the source_args key mounts
The docker source accepts the source_args key ports
The docker source accepts the source_args key network
The docker source accepts the source_args key cpus
The docker source accepts the source_args key memory
source_args are templated against scenario variables ({{scenario.<key>}}) before Open() is called
Example: source-backed mcp_servers entry (source docker, scope session, source_args image, repo, branch) is valid
Tools from a source-backed server are registered under their raw MCP names (Read, Edit) rather than mcp__<server>__<tool>
runtime.evals is a field under spec
runtime.evals binds an eval type name to a program on the host, and pack_evals references that type
The usual pack_evals trigger is on_session_complete
Arena runs a runtime eval program after the agent finishes and before the session's sandbox container is removed
A runtime eval program runs on the host, not inside the sandbox, so the agent cannot see it
A runtime eval program inherits the host environment, including Docker access
Example: runtime.evals sandbox_probe block with mcp_servers sandbox and pack_evals entry is valid
runtime.evals timeout_ms defaults to 30s (30000 ms) per invocation
pack_evals params are passed to the program as-is
pack_evals is a field
pack_evals[].id is a field
pack_evals[].type is a field
pack_evals[].trigger is a field
pack_evals[].params is a field
runtime.evals.<name>.command is the program to run
A relative command path containing / resolves against the config directory; a bare name is looked up on PATH
runtime.evals.<name>.args is an extra-arguments field
runtime.evals.<name>.env is a list of host environment variable names passed through to the program
The program inherits the rest of the host environment in addition to the env list
runtime.evals.<name>.timeout_ms is a per-invocation timeout field
runtime.evals timeout_ms default is 30000
On timeout or non-zero exit the eval scores 0 and stderr goes into the explanation
The runtime eval input is one JSON document on stdin
Example: runtime eval stdin JSON document (type, params, content, context) is well-formed
The runtime eval input has a top-level type field
The runtime eval input has a top-level params field
The runtime eval input content is the last assistant message
The runtime eval input has a top-level context object
context.session_id is the run id
context.messages is a field of the runtime eval input
context.tool_calls is a field of the runtime eval input
context.metadata is a field of the runtime eval input
context.metadata.arena is a field of the runtime eval input
metadata.arena.run_id is a field
metadata.arena.scenario_id is a field
metadata.arena.provider_id is a field
metadata.arena.region is a field
metadata.arena.trial_index is a field
metadata.arena.labels is a field
metadata.arena.artifacts_dir is a field
metadata.arena.sandboxes is a field
Each sandboxes entry has a container_id field
Each sandboxes entry has ports keyed by port, each with host_port and url fields
sandboxes is keyed by mcp_servers name
ports lists each port under the source's ports arg
artifacts_dir is a host directory for the run's outputs
The session_end workspace-capture hook writes into artifacts_dir
The workspace path inside the container depends on the image; it is /workspace for codegen-sandbox
A runtime eval program writes one JSON document to stdout
The runtime eval output has a score field
The runtime eval output has a detail field
The runtime eval output has a metrics field
The runtime eval output has a data field
The output score becomes the eval's score
The output metrics become the eval's named sub-scores
The output data becomes the eval's details in the run JSON
In the CSV export, each metric and each top-level numeric or boolean data entry gets an eval.<id>.<key> column
Nested values in data stay in the run JSON and are not exported to CSV
An output of the form {error: ...} records the eval as errored rather than as a score of 0
A crash, a timeout, or output that is not valid JSON counts as an error
Runtime eval programs should write logs to stderr
Session evals run once per session, after the agent's last turn, while the sandbox container is still running
Session evals run even when the run is cut off by tool_policy.max_rounds, tool_policy.max_cost_usd or defaults.run_timeout
tool_policy.max_rounds is a field
tool_policy.max_cost_usd is a field
After a run timeout, session evals run on a fresh context bounded by their own timeout_ms
The session_end hook runs after the session evals, and the container is removed last
A session eval program can docker exec into the sandbox container
skills is a field name in the config
Skills are mounted into the sandbox, where the agent can read them
Link: examples/sandbox-host-eval/ example directory exists in the repo
pack_metadata.governance is a field
packc compile copies the governance block into the pack's metadata.governance
agents.members.<name>.governance is a field that can declare an agent-level governance block
A field set in an agent's governance block replaces the pack value; a field left out inherits it
governance.accountable_owner is a string field
governance.autonomy_level is a string field
governance.autonomy_level enum values are suggests, acts_with_approval, acts_with_oversight, acts_autonomously
governance.intended_purpose is a string field
governance.foreseeable_misuse is an array of strings
governance.operator_role is a string field
governance.risk_classification is a string field
operator_role and risk_classification accept a vocabulary term such as eu-aiact:AIDeployer or a free string
governance.intended_deployment_contexts is an array of strings
governance.capabilities is an array of strings
governance.approved_environments is an array of strings
governance.requires_ai_disclosure is a bool field
governance.vocabularies is an object mapping a CURIE prefix to an IRI
Well-known vocabulary prefixes include dpv, eu-aiact, ai, pp and risk
governance.extensions is an opaque object of annotations
governance.obligations is an array field
Each obligation has an id
Each obligation has an obligation term
Obligation applies_to is optional, with enum values capability, data_class, risk_classification
Each obligation has optional note and extensions fields
Each obligation has a controls field
Each control has exactly one key
A control key field names a governance field that must be declared
A control key validator is the id of a validator on one of the pack's prompts
A control key eval is the id of a pack eval or a prompt eval
A control key external describes a control outside the pack in prose
governance.reviews is an array field
Each review has an id
Each review has a type term
Each review has a cadence that is an ISO 8601 duration such as P3M
Each review has an owner team
A review has an optional satisfies list of obligation ids
A review has an optional eval field
A review has an optional extensions field
governance.independent_of is an object field
independent_of.axes accepts model, provider, tools, prompts and accountable_owner
independent_of.enforcement enum values are strict and advisory
independent_of requires that whatever produces the agent's input differ from the agent on the listed axes
Example: pack_metadata.governance block (obligations, controls, reviews) is valid
promptarena validate and packc compile check governance references
A control naming a validator, eval or field the pack does not declare is an error
A review naming an obligation that does not exist is an error
An obligation or review term whose prefix is neither well-known nor declared in vocabularies is a warning
The governance block, prompt specs, validators, pack evals, workflow states, agent members, compositions and tools each accept extensions
Nothing in PromptArena or PromptKit interprets extensions
Link: mortgage underwriting example at /arena/examples/mortgage-underwriting/ carries a complete governance block
defaults.output is the output configuration section for test results
defaults.output.dir is a string output directory path
defaults.output.formats is an array of output formats
The json output format writes a JSON results file
The markdown output format writes a Markdown report
The markdown report default output path is out/results.md
The junit output format writes JUnit XML
html is accepted as an alias for the markdown output format
defaults.output.recording is an object field
defaults.output.recording.enabled is a bool field
defaults.output.recording.enabled defaults to false
defaults.output.recording.dir is a string field
defaults.output.recording.dir defaults to recordings
Session recording captures detailed event streams for each test run, including audio data for voice conversations
Link: Session Recording Guide at /arena/how-to/scenarios/session-recording/
defaults.fail_on is an array field of conditions that cause test failure
defaults.fail_on is an array of failure conditions
fail_on value assertion_failure means any assertion fails
fail_on value provider_error means the provider API returns an error
fail_on value timeout means the test exceeds its configured timeout
fail_on value validation_error means a validator or guardrail triggers
PromptConfig is a configuration kind
A PromptConfig defines a prompt's system instructions, validators and metadata
Example: PromptConfig structure block (metadata, labels, spec) is valid
PromptConfig apiVersion is promptkit.altairalabs.ai/v1alpha1
PromptConfig kind is PromptConfig
PromptConfig metadata.labels is a field
spec.task_type is a required string field
spec.version is an optional semantic version string
spec.description is an optional string field
spec.system_template is a required field of PromptConfig
Prompt spec accepts an optional `validators` array of runtime validators/guardrails
Validator type `banned_words` exists and takes params `words` and `message`
Validator type `max_length` exists
max_length validator params are `max_characters`, `max_tokens`, `message`
Prompt spec accepts an `allowed_tools` list of tool names
allowed_tools names tools registered under the arena config's spec.tools, or MCP tools as mcp__<server>__<tool>
A prompt with no allowed_tools gets no tools
allowed_tools is what grants a particular prompt access to a tool registered with the arena
A system_template that mentions tools while allowed_tools is empty leaves the model with an instruction it cannot carry out
If the provider declares a capabilities list, it must include `tools` for tool use to be permitted
Prompt spec has a `task_type` field that categorizes the prompt's purpose
Common task_type value `general` (general-purpose assistant)
Common task_type value `support` (customer support)
Common task_type value `creative` (content generation)
Common task_type value `analysis` (data/text analysis)
Common task_type value `code` (code generation/review)
Common task_type value `qa` (question answering)
system_template is the system prompt sent to the LLM and supports {{variable_name}} substitution
Variables are substituted when the prompt is assembled
Variables can be overridden in arena.yaml via prompt_configs[].vars
Prompt spec has a `variables` array of variable definitions with metadata
Variables are referenced in system_template with {{variable_name}} syntax
Variable field `name` is a required string
Variable field `type` is a required string
Variable type value `string`
Variable type value `number`
Variable type value `boolean`
Variable type value `array`
Variable type value `object`
Variable field `required` is a required boolean
Variable field `default` is optional, of any type, and applies to non-required variables
Variable field `description` is an optional string
Variable field `example` is an optional value of any type
Variable field `validation` is an optional object with rules pattern, minLength, maxLength, min, max
Required-variables example YAML (customer_id, account_type with pattern, max_retries with min/max) is valid against the variables schema
Optional-variables example YAML (company_name, support_tier, response_timeout, features_enabled with array default) is valid against the variables schema
arena.yaml prompt_configs example with id, file and vars overriding variable defaults is valid
prompt_configs[] entries accept a `vars` map
prompt_configs[] entries accept an `id` field
prompt_configs[] entries accept a `file` field
Required variables must be provided in arena.yaml prompt_configs[].vars, at runtime via SDK/API, or through scenario-specific configuration
Optional variables fall back to their defaults when not provided
Link to the Validators Reference at /arena/reference/validators/
Validator item field `id` is optional and is what a governance control refers to
Validator item field `type` names the validator
Validator item field `params` holds validator parameters
Validator item field `message` is an optional description
Validator item field `extensions` holds opaque annotations
Validator ids must be unique across the pack
Scenario example uses apiVersion promptkit.altairalabs.ai/v1alpha1 and kind Scenario
Scenario spec.task_type is required and must match the prompt's task_type
Scenario spec.description is an optional string
Assertion type `content_includes` takes a `patterns` list param
Assertion type `content_matches` takes a `pattern` param
Assertion type `tools_called` takes a `tools` list param
Scenario turns are a list where each turn is a scripted user message, an assistant message, or a self-play turn
Scripted turn field `role` is a required string set to user or assistant
Scripted turn role value `user`
Scripted turn role value `assistant`
Scripted turn field `content` is a required string
Scripted turn field `assertions` is optional and applies to user turns only
Scripted turn field `chaos` is an optional object for injecting tool failures
Self-play turn field `role` is a required string matching a configured role in self_play.roles
Self-play turn field `persona` is a required persona ID string
Self-play turn field `turns` is an optional int giving number of exchanges
Self-play turn field `turns` defaults to 1
Self-play turn field `max_turns` is an optional int upper bound on turns
When max_turns > turns, natural termination is enabled and the self-play LLM can end the conversation after the minimum turns
A user turn triggers LLM generation and its assertions check the response
An assistant turn provides context and does no LLM generation
A self-play turn generates user messages via a persona LLM, each triggering an assistant response
Link to the Assertions Reference at /arena/reference/assertions/
Assertion items have fields type, params and message
Scenario `context` is a free-form key-value map
Scenario context_metadata has typed fields domain and user_role; project_stage is accepted, unread, and warned about at load
A scenario with `data` runs once per row of its dataset file
A scenario cannot set both `data` and turn `perturbations`
data.file is a required string path to the dataset file
data.file has no default and is required
data.file accepts the extensions .jsonl, .ndjson and .csv
Relative data.file paths resolve against the scenario file, or against the arena config file for inline scenario_specs entries
data.field is an optional JSONL-only string that unwraps each row to the object under that key
data.field defaults to none
JSONL files must contain exactly one JSON object per line
Blank JSONL lines are skipped
JSONL numbers keep their written form (1.50 stays 1.50)
JSONL null values become empty strings
JSONL arrays and objects become compact JSON strings
CSV files use the first record as the header
Every CSV header column needs a unique, non-empty name
Every CSV record must have as many fields as the header
A leading UTF-8 byte order mark is removed from CSV files
{column} placeholders are replaced in turn content, text parts, assertion params and message, conversation_assertions, seed_memories content, and variables values
A placeholder column name starts with a letter or _ and continues with letters, digits, _, - or .
Double-braced {{name}} template variables are left for the prompt template
Substituted placeholder values are strings and are not scanned for further placeholders
Substituted values are inserted as written, so regex metacharacters in a value keep their regex meaning
A row's `id` column names the row; rows without one are named by their 1-based position
Two rows with the same ID is an error
The config fails to load when the dataset file has no rows
The config fails to load when a JSONL line is not a JSON object
The config fails to load when a placeholder the scenario uses has no column in some row
Each dataset row is a separate run per provider and region
With trials, every row runs that many times, and trial results and pass_threshold aggregate within the row
Reports name a row's runs scenario[row-id]
Each data row run carries the label `data_row: <row-id>`
The JSON result records Params.data_row and the row's values under Params.data
Dataset example (trials: 2, data.file data/capitals.jsonl, {country} and {answer} placeholders) is valid
trial_budget stops a scenario's trials early once one achieves its objectives or once the trials have cost a set amount
trial_budget field `stop_on_achieved` is a bool
trial_budget.stop_on_achieved defaults to false
stop_on_achieved starts no more trials once one has achieved every objective, and needs a turn with an objective
trial_budget field `max_cost_usd` is a number
trial_budget.max_cost_usd defaults to none
max_cost_usd starts no more trials once finished trials have cost at least this many USD
trial_budget example (trials: 20, stop_on_achieved: true, max_cost_usd: 2.00) is valid
The trial budget applies separately to each group of provider, region and dataset row
A budgeted group's trials run in order on one worker regardless of --concurrency
promptarena run accepts a --concurrency flag
max_cost_usd is checked between trials, so the trial that crosses it finishes and the group can overshoot by up to one trial's cost
A trial counts as achieved only when it achieves every objective it records, whatever each objective's expect
An objective on a turn whose persona invented a specific does not count toward achieved
trial_budget needs trials greater than 1 and at least one of its fields set
trial_budget cannot be combined with turn perturbations
Skipped trials are not counted in pass_threshold pass rates, objective attempts, or cost
The JSON result records trial_results.budget with trials_run, trials_skipped, stopped_by and trials_to_first_achieved
trial_results.budget stopped_by value `achieved`
trial_results.budget stopped_by value `max_cost`
stopped_by is absent when every trial ran
Link to the objectives report at /arena/reference/output-formats/#objectives-format
The objectives report shows how many groups got through, the mean trials taken, and the trials skipped
Under stop_on_achieved a group stops at its first success, so a success rate over the trials that ran overstates the per-trial rate
A turn field `perturbations` maps placeholder names to lists of values and runs the scenario once per combination
perturbations has type map of string to list of strings
perturbations defaults to none
perturbations maps each placeholder name to its candidate values
Perturbation keys are collected from every turn, and a key defined on several turns takes the union of its values
Perturbation variants are the Cartesian product of all keys, so {city: [NYC, LA], tone: [formal, casual]} gives four variants
{key} is replaced in the content and text parts of every turn, and assertions are not substituted
Per provider and region a perturbed scenario runs trials x variants times, and trial i uses variant i mod variants
All perturbation variants aggregate into one trial result
Perturbations example (city and tone placeholders on a user turn) is valid
A turn field `chaos` makes calls to named tools fail during that turn
chaos.tool_failures is a list of failure rules
chaos.tool_failures defaults to none
For each tool call, the first rule naming that tool whose probability roll fires is applied
tool_failures[].tool is a required string naming the tool to fail
tool_failures[].mode is a required string
tool_failures[].mode value `error`
tool_failures[].mode value `timeout`
tool_failures[].mode value `slow`
tool_failures[].probability is a number
tool_failures[].probability defaults to 1.0
A probability of 0 or unset means every call fails
tool_failures[].message is an optional string text the model receives
tool_failures[].message defaults per mode
The error and timeout modes block the call, so the tool never runs
The model receives a tool result of the form `Tool <name> blocked by hook: <message>`
Without a message, the default text is `Chaos: tool <name> failed with injected error` or `Chaos: tool <name> timed out (injected)`
The timeout mode does not exercise a real timeout; no time passes
The slow mode waits 2 seconds, then lets the call run normally
Any other mode blocks the call like error, with default text `Chaos: tool <name> failed (mode=<mode>)`
The chaos mode value is not validated
Injected tool result metadata carries chaos_injected: true, chaos_mode and chaos_tool
slow adds chaos_delay_ms to metadata, and timeout adds chaos_timeout: true
A blocked tool call fails the no_tool_errors assertion
A blocked tool call does not count as a call for tools_called
Scripted user turns and self-play turns honour chaos; duplex turns ignore it
Only tool calls made while that turn runs are affected by its chaos
Chaos example (lookup_order, mode error, probability 0.5, message) is valid
Provider example YAML (apiVersion, kind Provider, spec fields type, model, base_url, headers, credential, platform, defaults, pricing, capabilities, unsupported_params, additional_config) is valid
Provider manifests use apiVersion promptkit.altairalabs.ai/v1alpha1 and kind Provider
Provider spec.type is a required string naming the provider type
Provider spec.model is a required string naming the model
Provider spec.base_url is an optional API endpoint override
Provider spec.headers is a map of custom HTTP headers injected into every request
Custom headers that collide with built-in headers such as Authorization or Content-Type are rejected at request time with an error
Provider spec.credential is an optional object holding credential configuration
credential.api_key is a direct API key field (not recommended)
credential.credential_file is a path to a file containing the API key
credential.credential_env is the name of an environment variable holding the API key
Provider spec.platform is an optional object for cloud-hosted platform configuration
platform.type is an optional string
platform.type value `bedrock`
platform.type value `vertex`
platform.type value `azure`
platform.region is an AWS/GCP region string
platform.project is the GCP project ID, used for Vertex only
platform.endpoint is a custom endpoint URL, used for Azure
Provider spec.defaults holds model parameters temperature, top_p and max_tokens
defaults.temperature is the sampling temperature
defaults.temperature range is 0.0 to 2.0
defaults.top_p is the nucleus sampling value
defaults.top_p range is 0.0 to 1.0
defaults.max_tokens is the maximum response length
Provider spec.include_raw_output is a boolean that includes raw API responses in output
include_raw_output defaults to false
Provider spec.pricing is an optional object of cost overrides
pricing.input_per_1k is the cost per 1K input tokens

a persona ending the conversation in a rewound exchange does not end the turn
an exchange that achieves the objective is never rewound, nor one with a failed turn assertion or guardrail result
after a rewind, objective_feedback and success_checks describe the conversation without the removed exchange
the objective result rewinds detail lists exchange, message, response, checks and cost_usd for each rewind
objective field search explores a tree of conversations, keeping the best-scoring branches
each exchange, every kept branch has the persona draft branching candidate messages from its own conversation
with prune_off_topic the judge drops drafts that drifted off the objective before they are sent
the width best-scoring branches continue, and the search stops at the first branch whose success checks all pass or after depth exchanges
example search uses expect not_achieved, a content_includes success, strategy tree, branching 3, width 4, depth 5, judge scorer and prune_off_topic true
search field strategy is required
search strategy accepts only tree
search field branching defaults to 3
search field width defaults to 4
search field depth defaults to 5
search depth replaces the turn's turns and max_turns, and config rejects those alongside search
search field judge names a judge in spec.judges
the search judge scores each reply from 1 (nothing towards the objective) to 10 (meets it)
search field prune_off_topic defaults to false
prune_off_topic needs a judge
a branch whose success checks all pass scores 10 and ends the search
without a judge a non-success reply scores 1 + 8 x (checks passed / checks)
a judge score is capped at 9 for non-success replies and never stands in for the success checks
branches are ranked by score and ties keep the earlier branch
each draft is written from its branch's conversation with that branch's search_score and search_branch variables
persona state is forked per branch, and a branch whose state meets a stop_when condition is not extended
with a seed, each draft gets the next seed so siblings do not repeat each other
the run's conversation is the achieving branch, or else the best-scoring branch with the deeper one winning ties
search cost is listed in the cost breakdown under capability search, and judge calls are not costed
the objective result search detail gives the search configuration and what it did
search detail nodes counts branches sent to the agent and scored
search detail pruned_off_topic counts drafts the judge dropped before sending
search detail depth_reached is the deepest exchange sent to the agent
search detail best_score is the highest score any branch reached
search detail attacker_calls counts drafts written
search detail target_calls counts messages sent to the agent
search detail judge_calls counts judge calls
search detail judge_errors counts failed judge calls
a failed judge score falls back to the success checks, and a failed on-topic check keeps the draft
the objectives report totals the search details per group in a Tree search column
a search sends at most depth x width x branching messages to the agent
the search defaults allow up to 60 messages per run
search cannot be combined with rewind or with stop_on_success false
tree search branches run one at a time
on a streaming scenario a search turn runs without streaming
examples/tap-search runs a tree search on mock providers
defaults.output.dir is the output directory for results, media and recordings; run --out overrides it and serve reads results from it
judge: <name> selects a judge from spec.judges; an unknown name is a load error
A tool that sets a static mock result and a mock template fails to load
mode: exec is not available in PromptArena; a run stops at startup with the ErrInvalidToolMode message
Scenario context is not read by a run; only prompt-debug reads its user_context key
promptarena validate warns when scenario context has a variables key

Arena checks each pack_evals entry at engine build (id present and unique, type and trigger required with a valid trigger, sample_percentage 0-100, valid metric name/type/labels); a bad entry stops the run with 'invalid pack_evals'
A persona file accepts only keys in the persona schema; an unknown key, or more than one YAML document, fails the load

Scenario spec.providers is an optional list of provider ids restricting the scenario to those arena providers; when empty the scenario uses its provider_group (default unless set), or every provider if the group has none; validate reports an unknown id as an error listing the known ids
mode: local is not available in PromptArena: validate reports it as an error and run stops at startup on it
